title: Al-Haqq, the Truth
tomorrow: Amira has done all she can. what does she do with the wait?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ash-Shahid, the Witness, and the line: witnessed. Present for the whole morning, not just question two. Today, a question about one small word that wasn't quite true.

Her dad asked how the interview went. Amira said great! with an exclamation point, and went upstairs. It wasn't great. It was medium: one strong answer, one blank, a decent ending. The truth would have taken four more words. Small round-ups like that are easy to say. Fine. Great. Almost done. Nobody gets hurt. But underneath sits an older question: what does truth have to do with God?
screen: `GREAT! (IT WAS MEDIUM.)` → `FINE. GREAT. ALMOST DONE.` → `WHAT DOES TRUTH HAVE TO DO WITH GOD?`

segments.voice: The Qur'an's answer is that truth isn't only something you say. It's one of God's Names. Surah Al-Hajj: "That is because Allah, He is the Truth." Al-Haqq: the Truth, the Real, the one who needs no rounding up. And in Surah Al-Isra: "Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish." Falsehood has no staying power. The Real does. A neighbor tradition says something close, in its own words. In the Talmud, in tractate Shabbat, Rabbi Hanina teaches that the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth: emet, in Hebrew. A seal is a signature, the mark pressed onto a finished thing. And a midrash notices that emet is spelled with the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, one from the middle, and the last, as if truth runs the whole way through. Here's the shared ground: both traditions tie truth to God, not just to good manners. And the honest difference: in Islam, al-Haqq is a Name you can call on directly, ya Haqq. In that Talmud passage, truth is God's seal, the mark on His work, rather than a Name to call. Two ways of honoring what's real. Here's the thought to tell a friend tonight: if truth runs from first letter to last, it runs through small words too. A tiny great! isn't a crime. It's just a chance to say the real thing instead.
screen: `ALLAH, HE IS THE TRUTH.` · `FALSEHOOD IS BOUND TO VANISH.` · `THE TALMUD: GOD'S SEAL IS EMET.` · `A NAME TO CALL, A SEAL ON HIS WORK.` · then, large: `THE TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Write down one true sentence you've been rounding off: not great, medium; not fine, tired; not almost done, haven't started. Read it once, quietly, out loud, and notice how the true sentence sounds in your own voice. If it belongs to someone, it can reach them later. For now, let the sit hold it.

segments.voice: Al-Haqq. The Truth, the Real, a Name you can call on, and the one thing that doesn't vanish. Name fifty-one.
Your line: the truth, which lasts when the round-ups don't, from the first letter to the last. See you tomorrow.
